note: Palle, 2026-11-15: 'Think of what we can represent the artifact and maps as: a playground, prefab assemblages, robotic unit stations, 3D mind mapping, a hero artifact, biomes etc.' This is the pass's answer as data: six forms an idea can take in the tower, what each is good for, what makes it, and the test for choosing it; then, hall by hall for the foundations crisis, which forms stand, which are written and which are only a guess from the hall's name (marked so: a guess is to be read against the hall's text and its works' code before anything is built). An idea usually wants two or three forms, not one: a hero to point at, a mind map to say what it means, and one form a body or a machine actually does. tools/arguments.py --check holds every visual argument's 'form' against this list.

forms.is: One work per hall staged as the centre: a ring of tape, two work lights, every thread tied back to it.
forms.good_for: Saying which work carries the hall's sentence. Without it a floor of ten works has no first thing to look at.
forms.made_with: argument_floor's hero (ring, work lights from the catalogue); the hall's own artifact, not a new one.
forms.test: If only this one work stood on the floor, would the hall still say its sentence?

forms.is: The working-out in language: cardboard plates in marker, stickers, red threads with a word each, the same words on text tape along the floor.
forms.good_for: Relations between ideas, wrong turns, what something is NOT, open questions. The layer that says what the other forms mean.
forms.made_with: commons/data/arguments/<hall>.json; the sticker app (readings, hanging boards, later cardboard constructions); the tape rolls' printed strip.
forms.test: Is there something here that can only be said, not done or shown? Then it belongs on a plate. Keep the plates few.

forms.is: The idea as something a body undergoes: a loop, a limit, a one-way, a climb, a floor that changes under you.
forms.good_for: Constraints and impossibilities that are felt before they are understood: you cannot get back, it never closes, there is always one more step.
forms.made_with: the place kit (playground_spec_hall, place_spec) and walkable prefab scenes through prefab_city.gd (wedges, gates, decks, water).
forms.test: Can the visitor's own walk be the argument - and does the tower's walker fail or succeed in the way the idea says?

forms.is: The idea built from the tower's real parts so that it can be counted, rearranged, taken apart: a grid of panels, nested fences, a row of crates.
forms.good_for: Ideas about collections, construction and totality: what is on the list, what is built from what, what is left outside.
forms.made_with: the spatial lab's inputs through lab_input.gd / prefab_city.gd; forms bred in the breeding yard (ada_run/bred_prefabs).
forms.test: Is the idea about things and their arrangement? Then every thing in it should be a part someone could pick up.

forms.is: A machine doing a procedure without us: bringing, checking, sorting, laying, for as long as it runs.
forms.good_for: Rules, searches and checks - and what a rule does when nobody interprets it. A robot can be wrong, slow or stuck in ways a diagram cannot.
forms.made_with: kinematic stations from prefabs (checking_station); the Unit's drones where their model fits; always the hall's own model for the procedure.
forms.test: Is the idea about what a procedure can and cannot establish by running? Then let one run, and count honestly what it has established.

forms.is: Something that grows and is not finished: the tower's living layer inside a bounded place.
forms.good_for: Ideas about becoming, about what is not decided in advance, and about living with what does not resolve.
forms.made_with: biome_box (the biome in a glass grid box), the nature system; a live work under a body must ask to be woken.
forms.test: Does the idea deny that everything is already there? Then show something that is still arriving.

halls.why: Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the postulates plaque, ringed, straight ahead of the arrival), the mind map (seven plates from the plaque past the lines and the triangle to the lane, and the hanging board arg_euclid), the playground (meeting_point: the fifth postulate the length of the slab - every line through P that falls short has a meeting that can be walked to, and the body's own line has one that runs off the building as the body steps toward the gold line), and two standing words, PARALLEL and GIVEN. Written, not built: three wedges on one straight line (Euclid I.32 at body size).

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the triangle bench, moved onto the slab beside the arrival - it stood in the air beyond the south edge), the mind map (seven plates from the arrival to the dome, the disk and the surfaces, and the hanging board arg_noneuclid), the playground (the walked triangle: the tutorial's own record of three pairs read as a sphere on a walkable dome and as a plane on a mat), and two standing words facing each other across the floor, STRAIGHT and 180. The biome guessed from the name was dropped: the text is about the rule for 'straight' and about models on an ordinary floor, not about growth. Added the same day: the hall's own wing, Seven Spaces (a stencil doorway and twelve spaces behind it), was moved clear of a column that kept every visitor out; and a second playground, cornered_block - three right-angled corners close a walk on flat floor (270), the excess at one point inside the block. And a third: mirror_lap - a corridor joined to itself the other way up; one lap and the word LEFT is on your right, reading backwards. And a fourth: walked_tiling - a deck that draws a floor of five squares to a corner round the walker; a square walk that closes on the slab leaves home 2.4 m away. And the biome after all, on Palle's word: small_planet - a world ten metres across reached by a door, with grass, trees and beetles that walk great circles; walk straight and the door comes back.

Gone back to on 11-16 with what the later floors taught. Standing: the hero (the workbench at the arrival), the mind map (ten plates, stickers, tape, the hanging board), a prefab assemblage (the grid and the row that is not on it), a playground (in_and_out: the workbench's two buttons as two gates on one railed corridor, where each answer is sent to the other and a body can walk out; WITHIN U takes away one rail beside OUT) and a second assemblage (fence_beyond: a yard of four things and the one thing outside it; FENCE IT IN builds the next fence, inside goes 4, 5, 6, 7 and outside stays 1; the fourth fence is tape). The four works that stood in corner columns stand by the middle of the floor in the order the text meets them. Landmarks: the standing words ERROR, NULL, INFINITY.

Gone back to on 11-16 with what the later floors taught. Standing: the hero (the provability sorter, straight ahead of the arrival), the mind map (ten plates, stickers, tape, the hanging board), a robot station (the checking station: slow and impossible look alike from outside), and a playground (gap_moves_up: four rising landings round the incompleteness tower itself; a plate lays the planks across a gap, the sentence is an axiom, and the next gap is one level up; the fourth landing ends at tape with the next sentence straight above where the walk began; gaps open reads 1 at every stage). The eight works that stood in columns stand where the text meets them: the machine east of the sorter, the plaque by the word PROVABLE, the four checking works in a row on the north-east, the picture by the shaft that is the way down. Landmarks: the standing words TRUE and PROVABLE on the two wings.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the small staircase, brought from the far edge to the arrival, ringed), the mind map (eight plates from the staircase past the beams, the trident and the pipe to the roof's door, and the hanging board arg_escher), the playground (roof_stair: a door onto a roof drawn like a print where wide steps go up on all four sides and bring you back - the other agreement the hall names, a moved room), and two standing words, UP and AGAIN. Built and taken off the floor again: the cardboard stairwell (endless_stair).

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the choice bench, brought from the far corner to the arrival, ringed), the mind map (eight plates from the bench past the spheres, the cube and the diagonal bench to the north edge, and the hanging board arg_brouwer), the playground (made_walk: the row as a walkway over the edge that grows only by the walker's choices, and beside it one laid by a clock), and two standing words, WAIT and WITNESS. No robot station after all: the hall's point is that nothing runs unless you choose, and a machine that ran would have been the clock's side of it - which is what the second walkway is.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the both-true gate, brought from the far corner to straight ahead of the arrival and walked through, ringed), the mind map (eight plates from the gate past the sphere to the yard and the box at the back, and the hanging board arg_florensky), the playground (consequence_yard: seven doors with a sentence over each; hold both reports and five open under four values, all seven classically - explosion as something a body can do), and two standing words, BOTH and ANYTHING. No biome: what the hall keeps unresolved is two reports, and it is exact about what that does and does not license.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the formula, brought from the far edge to straight ahead of the arrival with its two sliders; the floor was restaged - the visitor used to arrive inside the atrium), the mind map (nine plates from the formula round the sliders, the diagram, the atrium, the returning works and the wall of the large sentence to the six cards and back, and the hanging board arg_synthesis), a robot station (six_cards: the hall's six cards at body size behind the wall; five run a check when stood before - refuted, searched to a budget, measured, exhibited, countermodelled - and the sixth, an AI's claim from the cardboard on these floors, runs nothing and says so), and two standing words, = and MAY. No playground: the hall gathers the earlier floors' works and asks what they warrant; a new thing to climb would have been one more unwarranted claim.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the console, qfep_balance_workbench, brought from the far north edge to straight ahead of the arrival and turned to face it, with the formula hung behind and above it as the hall text says, the two rails at either hand and the three spheres at the visitor's left), the mind map (nine plates from the console round the rails and the formula to the painted floor, and the hanging board arg_qfepintro), a playground (total_line: the console's question - can two different arrangements give the same number? - on a painted floor where a step east is F and a step north is E; the floor keeps a place, and a red line runs through every other place with that total), and two standing words, EQUAL and WHICH. No robot station: the console is one already, and the hall's point is what its one number leaves out.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the workbench, shannon_workbench, brought from the far north edge to straight ahead of the arrival and turned to face it; the film monitor, which stood 0.8 m in front of the arriving visitor's face, at the left hand; the lambda cabinet at the right), the mind map (nine plates from the workbench to the walk and its last plate, and the hanging board arg_qfepf), a playground (guessing_walk: the hall's prediction study with a body for a predictor - twelve hidden bits in two lanes, an amber bar for each bit that refuses the walker, AGAIN for the same bits, and one plate that changes the world instead, which is what the hall's last lines warn of), and two standing words, DIFFICULT and WHOSE. No robot station: the hall's point is that nothing here learns but whoever walks.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the fan, entropy_fan, brought from the far north edge to straight ahead of the arrival with its four buttons toward the visitor; the particle spray, which stood on the arrival point, on the west wing; four works off the columns they overlapped), the mind map (nine plates from the fan to the tree, its gates and its asked-for branch, and the hanging board arg_qfepe), a playground (drawn_tree: sixteen endings taped on the floor to be the traveller in - a walked path lights and hangs a bead; the entropy is given as counted and as walked; PRUNE A and B leave the same count and different endings; OPEN returns endings and not the beads; and a third way can be asked for at the last forks, which the fan cannot yet do), and two standing words, 81 and WHO. No robot station: the fan is the machine, and the hall's question is who may change what it draws.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the hall itself, lambda_hall, brought from the west wing, where a third of it hung past the south edge, to the middle of the floor: the arrival looks straight down its lit route, the recommendation console at the right hand and the chalkboard by the door; the small works in two rows outside the hall, regular side and dispersed side; the bifurcation walkway on the east wing), the mind map (nine plates round the hall from the door and the chalkboard to the far corner and the west wing, and the hanging board arg_qfeplambda), a playground (worn_path, on the west wing: a field of tiles that darken where feet go, three rows of posts with their gaps in line, a lit strip that plates move - a recommendation, an arrangement and a record of use, kept apart), and two standing words, LIT and BUILT, at the two ends of the east wing. No robot station: the hall's console is one, and its point is how little it moves.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the signed rail, phi_slider, brought from a column at the north edge to straight ahead of the arrival, the transforming pattern behind it, the preserved pattern beside that, the rigid and the fluid form at either hand, the promenade by shaft A; the sticker app's installation on this floor is another hand's and was not touched), the mind map (nine plates from the rail to the two patterns, the promenade and the track, none within a metre of the sticker installation, and the hanging board arg_qfepphi), a playground (signed_walk, in the band south of shaft B: a track read once a second, plates for the weight, and a stand that keeps the weight, the change and their product in three places), and two standing words north of shaft B, PLUS in front of a larger BETTER. No robot station: nothing on this floor hears the rail, and the hall says so.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the two-screen console, edge_of_chaos_unlocked, brought from a column on the east wing behind the arriving visitor to straight ahead of the arrival; the rail 'nearer the door' and wired to nothing; the funnel experiment, the Turing pattern and the core beside them; the particle field on the west wing), the mind map (nine plates from the console and the unconnected rail to the two spirals, and the hanging board arg_qfepedge), a playground (step_spiral: one rule, a circle round a pole, computed a step at a time from one start for one turn of model time in two step sizes - two spirals in stones and tape; a plate halves the steps, a wall clips them, a ball runs faster along the same stones), and two standing words, RULE and RUN. No robot station: the console is the machine, and the hall's question is what its run adds to its rule.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the reactor, qfep_reactor, with its two handles: brought from three corners of the north edge to one group ahead of the arrival, handles in front and receiver behind; the particle field that 'has not joined this connection' beside them; the formula off its column), the mind map (nine plates from the two handles and the reactor to the rail and the two gates, and the hanging board arg_qfepsandbox), a playground (offered_used: a rail whose value is offered, a gate that stands open by the value it uses, a route that can be made and cut; cut it and the gate keeps its last value; another mapping turns the consequence round; a second gate moves by itself), and two standing words, OFFERED and USED. No robot station: the reactor is one, and the hall's question is what reaches it.

Read on 11-15. Standing: the hero (the specimen in its jar, queer_morphology_specimen, brought from a column at the north edge to straight ahead of the arrival, with the formula above and behind it, the four spheres of its terms in a row under the formula, the meter and the ceiling at either hand), the mind map (nine plates from the jar to the mast, and the hanging board arg_qfepsynth), a robot station (asked_read_measured: a three-metre mast on a sprung foot; plates ask for stiffness, damping and drag; a stand keeps what was asked, what the property reads back and what was measured from the mast's motion in three columns, with the tip's trace under them; stiffness does nothing until REBUILD, drag is used by nothing, and steady is not still), and two standing words, STEADY and STILL, side by side on the east wing. No playground: the hall's question is what a body keeps, and the mast answers by being watched.

Read on 11-16. Standing: the hero (the table of twenty-four words, bias_from_inside, brought from eleven metres off to four metres ahead of the arrival; the two works that stood behind the arriving visitor turned to face them at either hand), the mind map (nine plates from the table to the two fields of posts, and the hanging board arg_critbias), a playground (room_to_tell_apart: twenty-four posts in two fields, a rail that presses the warm twelve to a fifth of their spread while the grey spread; a stand that counts present, room round it and hidden from where you stand; a pair can be kept by standing between it; another grouping makes another twelve warm), and two standing words, PRESENT and APART, facing each other across the floor. No robot station: the operation is one line of interpolation and the hall prints it.

Read on 11-16. Standing: the hero (the pedestal with the miniature rooms, room_shape_demonstrator, brought out from under the arriving visitor's feet to four metres ahead; the five works that stood in a row along the south edge set round it facing in), the mind map (nine plates from the pedestal to the two plans at full size, and the hanging board arg_critethics), a playground (seat_you_take: a long table with a head and a ring of six at full size; tapes at eye height between seats that face each other, half tapes where only one faces; the seat you stand on lights its own; NECK sets how far a neck turns and ANGLE THE CHAIRS turns the sides to the head), and two standing words, SPACED and HEARD, facing each other across the floor. No robot station: nothing here runs; the hall is about what stands before anyone speaks.

Read on 11-16. Standing: the hero (the two branches and their panel, merge_conflict_visualizer, brought from behind the arriving visitor's left shoulder, back turned, to straight ahead and facing them; the sphere, the three pillars, the workbench and the text panel set round them), the mind map (nine plates from the branches along the south band to the east wing, and the hanging board arg_specpara), a robot station (two_reports, on the east wing because the vault fills the middle: two report slips about a door, a classical and a paraconsistent reasoner that answer seven questions each with a lamp, two real doors of which one stands open and one is shut, and WHERE FROM? which gives each report its source, hour and door), and two standing words, OPEN and CLOSED, side by side on the west wing: both stand. No playground: the hall's own text asks for a rule table, and a rule table is a station.

Read on 11-16. Standing: the hero (the four inward-facing panels, situated_readout, which already stand round the arrival inside the camera bay: nothing of the installed bay is moved), the mind map (nine plates outside the bay: two at the south corners, three along the south band, four round the stations; and the hanging board arg_specsit), a robot station (four_stations, on the east wing: a field with a line, four corner stations that each see part of the visitor's walk and each mean something else by DANGEROUS; every station says what it saw, what the word means to it and its verdict; ONE DEFINITION and ONE RECORD split the disagreement into evidence and definition), and two standing words, SAW and MEANS, side by side on the west wing. No playground: the hall's own text proposes the experiment, and it is a set of measuring stations.

Read on 11-16. Standing: the hero (the growing helix with its twelve rim nodes and its panel, peer_production_tool, moved a metre and a half so that its panel is ahead of the arrival and its signs no longer cover the view; the round table beside it is the hall's second half and is not moved), the mind map (nine plates from the helix and the table to the marked floor, and the hanging board arg_speccoll), a playground (marks_and_walls: a field of cells with walls that cannot be seen and six sources' chalk marks, felt or told, some repeated, some wrong, some walls unmarked; the visitor's body checks, adds and strikes; a stand counts the marks and how many edges they are wrong about), and two standing words, COUNTED and CHECKED, facing each other across the floor. No robot station: the helix is one already, and the hall's question is what a body can check.

Read on 11-16. Standing: the hero (the walk-in cave, rhizome_cave_demo, which stood out over the void with nothing leading to it and a floor the tower did not accept as ground: it is not moved, its row gains exterior_walk; and the small grower the text meets 'near the way in', brought to straight ahead of the arrival with the film monitor beside it), the mind map (nine plates from the grower to the bridgehead and the gap on the east wing, and the hanging board arg_specrhiz), a prefab assemblage (way_round, from the lab's own planks and panels: a plank footbridge with staggered joints and plank rails into the cave's near mouth, and a panel gangway from its far mouth round its north-east corner and back down its east side, stopping 1.7 m short of the east wing; two plates lay or lift the last panel), and two standing words, SEE and ENTER, facing each other across the floor. No playground or station: the cave is the playground, and what it lacked was a way in.

Read on 11-16. Standing: the hero (the workshop of bodies, MolecularDesigner: the amber-jointed body, the assembly that finds its places, the other body over its mat and the furniture; moved as one to the middle of the floor ahead of the arrival; the three table pieces set at either hand), the mind map (nine plates round the workshop and along the south band to the west wing, and the hanging board arg_labequip), a playground (joint_more, on the west wing where there is more room: the workshop's body drawn on the floor six metres tall; standing still plants a joint, holding a joint chooses its neighbour, holding one and standing on another joins them; a stand keeps positions and neighbours as two lists and counts parts and loops), and two standing words, POSITION and NEIGHBOUR, side by side on the east wing. No robot station: the workshop's assembly is one already.

Read on 11-16. Standing: the hero (the two bodies, assembly_return: the blue starting pose and the bay for the last kept one, brought from eight metres off to five, with the ledger the text passes on the way ahead and to the left of the arrival, the formula above the bodies, and the works that stood in a row along the south edge set round them facing in), the mind map (nine plates from the bodies and the ledger to the line that keeps a walk, the ninth behind the arrival so that it is met on turning round; and the hanging board arg_postcrisis), a robot station (two_arrivals: a line from START to END; the last two walks kept in blue and amber; a stand that reads them as a destination and as a path; a plate that chooses what the next record holds; three words for a note), and two standing words, ARRIVED and MISSING, facing each other across the floor. No playground: the hall is about what a record keeps, and the recorder is a station.
